# Inherited slots and slot_usage

A class can get the metaslots of a slot from several places: its own `slot_usage`, the `slot_usage` of its parent classes and mixins, and the slot definition.
This page shows how ohi LinkML combines two kinds of them, where the LinkML specification, LinkML-Python 1.12.1 and ohi LinkML do not all agree:

- [Boolean metaslots](#boolean-metaslots), like `required` and `multivalued`, which are `true` or `false`.
  ohi LinkML follows the specification here, and LinkML-Python works differently.
- [Boolean expressions](#boolean-expressions): `any_of`, `all_of`, `exactly_one_of` and `none_of`, which are lists of conditions.
  ohi LinkML works differently from both the specification and LinkML-Python here.

It also shows what the generators do when a class changes an inherited slot in a way that their output can't express in the parent class: see [Slots that a class changes](#slots-that-a-class-changes).

## Boolean metaslots

The LinkML specification combines boolean metaslots, like `required` and `multivalued`, with OR when it derives a slot.
So a `slot_usage` can make a slot required or multivalued, but setting either to `false` has no effect when the slot or a parent class already sets it to `true`.
ohi LinkML does the same. LinkML-Python 1.12.1 uses the value from the closest `slot_usage` instead.

```yaml
classes:
  Base:
    slots:
      - name
      - tags
  Child:
    is_a: Base
    slot_usage:
      name:
        required: false
      tags:
        multivalued: false
slots:
  name:
    required: true
  tags:
    multivalued: true
```

| Slot of `Child` | LinkML-Python 1.12.1 | ohi LinkML |
|-----------------|----------------------|--------------|
| `name` | Optional | Required |
| `tags` | Single-valued | Multivalued |

So `{}` is a valid `Child` for `linkml-validate`, but not for the JSON Schema, SHACL, Pydantic or TypeScript that ohi LinkML generates.
To make a slot optional or single-valued in some classes, leave it optional or single-valued in the slot definition, and turn it on in the classes that need it.

## Boolean expressions

ohi LinkML combines the `any_of`, `all_of`, `exactly_one_of` and `none_of` lists of a slot so that a value of the class is also a valid value of each of its parent classes and mixins (Liskov substitution).

| Expression       | LinkML specification | LinkML-Python 1.12.1              | ohi LinkML                                                               |
|------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `all_of`         | Joins the lists      | Keeps only the most specific list | Joins the lists                                                            |
| `none_of`        | Joins the lists      | Keeps only the most specific list | Joins the lists                                                            |
| `any_of`         | Joins the lists      | Keeps only the most specific list | Keeps the most specific list, and requires the other lists too (see below) |
| `exactly_one_of` | Joins the lists      | Keeps only the most specific list | Keeps the most specific list, and requires the other lists too (see below) |

Joining the lists is correct for `all_of` and `none_of`: each member is one more check.
For `any_of` and `exactly_one_of`, neither joining nor keeping one list is correct:

- Joining `any_of` lists allows more values. A subclass can't narrow down the ranges.
- Keeping only the most specific `any_of` list allows a subclass to add ranges that a parent class doesn't allow.
- An `exactly_one_of` with fewer members can allow more values: a value that matches two inherited members is not valid for the parent class, but it is valid for a list with only one of these members.

So ohi LinkML keeps the most specific list, and adds each other list to `all_of`, as a member with this list as its `any_of` or `exactly_one_of`.
An `any_of` list is not added if it has all the members of the most specific list, because then it allows all the values that the most specific list allows.

```yaml
classes:
  Base:
    slots:
      - value
  Child:
    is_a: Base
    slot_usage:
      value:
        any_of:
          - range: integer
          - range: boolean

slots:
  value:
    any_of:
      - range: integer
      - range: string
```

| Value  | LinkML specification (`any_of` of `integer`, `string`, `boolean`) | LinkML-Python 1.12.1 (`any_of` of `integer`, `boolean`) | ohi LinkML (both `any_of` lists) |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| 42     | Valid                                                             | Valid                                                   | Valid                              |
| "abc"  | Valid                                                             | Invalid                                                 | Invalid                            |
| true   | Valid                                                             | Valid, but not valid for `Base`                         | Invalid                            |

For `Child.value`, ohi LinkML uses this derived slot:

```yaml
any_of:
  - range: integer
  - range: boolean
all_of:
  - any_of:
      - range: integer
      - range: string
```

The SHACL generator emits all of it.
The OWL generator gives each class its own `any_of` ranges; OWL subclassing requires the ranges of the parent classes too.
The JSON Schema and Pydantic generators do not support boolean expressions yet.

## Slots that a class changes

Some outputs pass what a parent class says about a field down to its subclasses: GraphQL interfaces, Scala abstract classes and traits, OWL class restrictions, and Pydantic classes.
A `slot_usage` can change a slot in a way that these outputs can't pass down:

```yaml
classes:
  Base:
    slots:
      - labels
  Child:
    is_a: Base
    slot_usage:
      labels:
        multivalued: true

slots:
  labels:
    range: string
```

In GraphQL, `Child` can't implement the `labels: String` field of `Base`'s interface with a list.
In OWL, `Child` can't drop the `owl:maxCardinality 1` that it inherits from `Base`.

So a parent describes a slot only when the versions of all its descendants fit.
Otherwise the descendants describe their own versions:

| Generator | When a descendant changes the slot's | Then |
|-----------|--------------------------------------|------|
| GraphQL   | name (`alias`), `multivalued`, or range to one that is not a subtype | The interface leaves out the field. Each type still has it. |
| Scala     | Scala type, for example with `required`, `multivalued` or a narrower class range | The abstract class or trait leaves out the `def`. Subclasses declare it where it fits all their descendants. |
| OWL       | `multivalued`, or range to one that is not derived from it | The class leaves out the `owl:maxCardinality 1` or the `owl:allValuesFrom`. Only the subclasses that keep it state it. |
| OWL       | `slot_uri` | The subclass declares the new property, and states all restrictions of the slot on it, including those from the `slot_usage` of its parents. |
| Pydantic  | JSON key (`alias`) | The subclass removes the inherited field, so loading rejects the old key. |

`validate` warns about a class that gives an inherited slot a range that is not derived from the parent's range.
See [Narrowing inherited ranges](200-limitations.md#narrowing-inherited-ranges).
